name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by {{field-1}} both sides of  the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}$ into the {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L5}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that {{field-4}} matrix.
worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}.$ To get $\text{L2},$ we are $\text{differentiating}$ with respect to $t$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}^{′}(t) & =(Φu(t))^{′} \\ {x}_{p}^{′}(t) & =Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L2},$ and $\text{L3}.$ Let's substitute ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$ from $\text{L1}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$ from $\text{L2}$ into the initial system of ODEs:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =Ax(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t) & =AΦu(t)+f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L3}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}$ into $\text{initial system of ODEs}.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L5}$ and $\text{L6}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are linearly independent. So, $Φ$ is invertible. Therefore, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L5}$ by $\text{pre-multiplying by }{Φ}^{-1}$ both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\cdot Φ{u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t) \\ ({Φ}^{-1}Φ)\cdot {u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t) \\ {u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

A derivation of the formula for xp(t) is given below.

L1: xp(t)=Φu(t)

L2: xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)

L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)

L4: Φ′=AΦ

L5: Φu′(t)=f(t)

L6: u′(t)=Φ−1(t)f(t)

L7: u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

L8: xp(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt

EXPLANATION

Let's examine each statement in turn.

  • We first consider lines L1 and L2. To get L2, we are differentiating with respect to t both sides of the equation in L1: xp′(t)=(Φu(t))′xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)

  • Next, we consider lines L1, L2, and L3. Let's substitute xp(t)=Φu(t) from L1 and xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t) from L2 into the initial system of ODEs: x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) Therefore, L3 is obtained by substituting L1 and L2 into initial system of ODEs.

  • Next, we consider lines L5 and L6. Since Φ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are linearly independent. So, Φ is invertible. Therefore, L6 follows from L5 by pre-multiplying by Φ−1 both sides of the equation: Φ−1⋅Φu′(t)=Φ−1⋅f(t)(Φ−1Φ)⋅u′(t)=Φ−1⋅f(t)u′(t)=Φ−1⋅f(t)

  • Finally, we consider line L4. Since Φ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t), i.e., by substituting any column c(t) of Φ into the homogeneous system, we get c′(t)=Ac(t), where c′(t) is the corresponding column of derivatives in Φ. As a result, this means that Φ′=AΦ. Therefore, L4 follows from the fact that Φ is a fundamental matrix.
